header.title: Hymn to Delos: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Callimachus
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg0533.tlg018.perseus-grc3, from the Perseus Digital Library (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0533.tlg018.perseus-: The name is Delos, 'visible', set against ἄδηλος, 'unseen'. The verb of the last clause (ἐξέφερον, 'were bearing') falls in the next line, so 'bore' is supplied in brackets.

nodes.text: But when you offered your soil for Apollo's birth,
the seafarers gave you this name in return,
because you no longer sailed about unseen, but in the waves
of the Aegean sea you planted the roots of your feet.
Nor did you shrink from Hera in her anger. She, at all
the women in childbed who [bore] children to Zeus, roared terribly,
